# Lamentations 1 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** How she-sits alone, the-city [once]-great with-people! She-has-become like-a-widow, [she who was]-great among-the-nations! A-princess among-the-provinces has-become forced-labor!

**2** She-weeps, yes-weeps in-the-night, and-her-tears [are] on her-cheek. There-is-none to-comfort-her among-all her-lovers; all her-friends have-dealt-treacherously with-her — they-have-become to-her enemies.

**3** Judah has-gone-into-exile from-affliction and-from-great servitude; she dwells among-the-nations — she-finds no rest; all her-pursuers overtook-her between-the-straits.

**4** The-roads-of Zion mourn, without-any-coming to [the]-appointed-feasts; all her-gates are-desolate, her-priests groan, her-virgins are-grieved, and-she — bitterness is-hers.

**5** Her-adversaries have-become [the]-head; her-enemies are-at-ease, for YHWH has-afflicted-her because-of the-multitude-of her-transgressions; her-young-children have-gone captive before the-adversary.

**6** And-departed from-[the]-daughter-of Zion all her-splendor; her-princes have-become like-deer [that]-find no pasture, and-they-went without-strength before the-pursuer.

**7** Jerusalem remembers in-the-days-of her-affliction and-her-wandering all her-precious-things which were from-days-of old; when her-people fell into-the-hand-of [the]-adversary and-none helped-her, the-adversaries saw-her [and]-mocked at-her-downfall.

**8** A-sin Jerusalem sinned — therefore she-has-become a-mockery; all who-honored-her despise-her, for they-saw her-nakedness; she-also groans and-turns-away.

**9** Her-uncleanness [was] in-her-skirts; she-did-not-consider her-latter-end, and-she-fell astoundingly — there-is-no-comforter for-her. "See, YHWH, my-affliction, for the-enemy has-magnified-himself!"

**10** His-hand the-adversary spread over all her-precious-things; for she-saw nations enter her-sanctuary — those-whom You-commanded, "They-shall-not enter into-Your-assembly."

**11** All her-people groan, seeking bread; they-gave their-precious-things for-food to-restore life. "See, YHWH, and-look, for I-have-become worthless."

**12** "Is-it-nothing to-you, all [who]-pass-by the-way? Look and-see if-there-is any-pain like-my-pain, which was-dealt to-me, which YHWH inflicted in-the-day-of His-burning anger.

**13** From-on-high He-sent fire into-my-bones, and-it-overcame-them; He-spread a-net for-my-feet, He-turned-me-back; He-made-me desolate — all the-day faint.

**14** The-yoke-of my-transgressions is-bound by-His-hand; they-are-woven-together — they-came-up upon my-neck; He-caused my-strength to-stumble; the-Lord gave-me into-hands I-cannot-withstand.

**15** The-Lord rejected all my-mighty-ones in-my-midst; He-proclaimed against-me an-appointed-time to-crush my-young-men; the-Lord trod [as in]-a-winepress the-virgin daughter-of Judah.

**16** For these [things] I weep; my-eye, my-eye runs-down [with]-water, for far from-me [is] a-comforter [who]-restores my-soul; my-sons are desolate, for the-enemy has-prevailed."

**17** Zion stretches-out her-hands — there-is-no-comforter for-her; YHWH commanded concerning Jacob — his-adversaries [surround]-him; Jerusalem has-become an-unclean-thing among-them.

**18** "Righteous [is] YHWH, for against-His-mouth I-rebelled. Hear, please, all [the]-peoples, and-see my-pain: my-virgins and-my-young-men went into-captivity.

**19** I-called to-my-lovers — they deceived-me; my-priests and-my-elders in-the-city perished while-they-sought food for-themselves to-restore their-life.

**20** See, YHWH, that distress [is]-to-me — my-inward-parts are-in-turmoil, my-heart is-overturned within-me, for I-have-surely-rebelled. Outside the-sword bereaves; inside [it is] like-death.

**21** They-heard that I groan — there-is-no-comforter for-me. All my-enemies heard-of my-calamity; they-rejoiced that You did-it. Bring the-day You-proclaimed, and-let-them-be like-me!

**22** Let-all their-evil come before-You, and-deal with-them as You-dealt with-me for-all my-transgressions; for many [are] my-groans, and-my-heart [is] faint."

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **1:1**: Ekhah — 'How!' The Hebrew title of the book. An exclamation of stunned grief. The acrostic structure (each verse begins with successive Hebrew letter) imposes literary order on chaos.

- **1:12**: Ha-yesh makhovim ke-makhovi — 'Is there any pain like my pain?' Personified Jerusalem speaks in first person. The shift from third to first person marks the poem's emotional intensification.

- **1:15**: Gat darakh — 'winepress He trod.' The winepress as image of divine judgment: blood pressed from grapes becomes a metaphor for blood pressed from a people.

— EMET
